color.truth: A colour value enters an encounter: a light, a surface, a position, a neighbour and a viewer. Implement each relation, then examine what the implementation leaves out.
color.qfep_connection: Color is a system stateâ€”part of the S term in QFEP. But unlike vectors, color is fundamentally perceptual: the same wavelength can appear different colors depending on surrounding context. Color reveals the gap between ontology (photons) and experience (qualia).

color.demonstration: Mix RGB to create colors. See how context changes perception. Watch gradients reveal interpolation. Paint and observe.
color.description: Add colour to familiar primitives and static transformations, then investigate it through illumination, wearing, authored bands, spatial samples, grid assignments, accumulating paint and glass architecture.
learning_objectives: Apply colour assignments to familiar primitives and static transforms; compare what stays the same before asking how colour is produced.
Relate coloured illumination to a receiving surface in the renderer.
Use RGB coordinates to change a preview and, where available, a hand or nail material.
Recognise rainbow bands as an authored construction rather than evidence of spectral simulation.
Read hue and saturation as functions of position; distinguish a field from its discrete samples.
Trace a grid colour rule from cell coordinates to per-instance colour values.
Compare manual and automatic marks accumulating on the same canvas.
Distinguish tinted-glass compositing from colour-coordinate interpolation.

Pattern_Foundry, Tutorial_Pattern, Array_Patterns and Symmetry_Seventeen are in tiling. 2026-09-23: author removed Chamber_Color from the active Colour sequence; its map, artifacts and writing remain available.

artifact_groups.rationale: MultiMesh color cycling test: pattern progression through flashlight interaction. Synthesis of color systems.
Nail salon studio: precise color selection on a digital body. Introduces color as interaction.
Walking through light: spectrum progression with animated rainbow emitters along a corridor.
Walk through a continuous spatial gradient sampled by 35 pillars, then compare twelve named palettes on a framed wall.
Grid becomes canvas: systematic color assignment cell by cell with spectrum visualization.
An automatic mark is already accumulating on the canvas; manual pigment and Albers studies remain available.
Eight full-size glass cubicles organise passage and layered views; contrast this with colour coordinates and interpolation.
